newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on Tokyo buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on Tokyo buying.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended slightly up on Thursday from its New York close on buying interest from the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) and good physical demand, gold traders said.
"There was good demand from Tokyo as the yen was stronger," one dealer at a European bank said.

Activity in the physical market remained relatively slow, with a movement limited to a HK$1 range, but gold traders said that a shortage of kilobars in Hong Kong had driven premiums up to U.S. cents 60-70 from U.S. cents 30-50 a month or so ago, industry sources said.
"People (from overseas) are calling and asking whether we need 9999 gold because everyone else here does," one gold trader said.
Players are covering their options positions, driving up volatilities slightly, said a trader at an international bank.
"But there won't be any large rallies until there is movement in the spot market," he noted.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) announced Wednesday it was committed to helping developing countries but stopped short of announcing gold sales.
"People are a little scared," the source said, noting the lack of clarity left the market uncertain about its direction.
Bullion ended at US$383.20/70 an ounce Thursday against New York's US$383.05/55 close on Wednesday.
Local gold ended HK$4 higher at HK$3,532 a tael.
The carry over charge dropped to -5 on Thursday compared to -4 on Wednesday.
